cushion.title: Top up your emergency cash
cushion.why: You have $19,000 today, covering only a little over one month while the plan recommends 8 to 9 months.
steps: Calculate your essential monthly expenses from recent bank statements
Decide one concrete target this month (one more month of expenses)
Transfer that amount into a separate savings account this month

retirement.title: Start retirement contributions to your 401(k)s
retirement.why: Your current contributions are $0 yet the plan projects $124,071 annual retirement need and employer matches could help.
steps: Contact each employer’s HR or benefits portal to confirm any match
Log into each 401(k) plan and choose an initial deferral
Set the deferral to start with the next payroll period

debt.title: Pay extra toward the 24.9% credit card
debt.why: One credit card charges 24.9% and, at current payments, won’t be paid off until January 2034.
steps: Check this month’s credit card statement for your current payment amount
Make a one-time extra payment toward the card this month
Adjust your monthly budget so a higher payment fits going forward

college.title: Discuss 529 funding versus other goals
college.why: You have $30,000 in 529s and add $8,000 a year, which competes with protection, cash, and retirement for the same free cash flow.
steps: Together list your yearly free cash flow available for goals
Confirm you currently add $8,000 a year to the 529s
Decide and implement one change to the 529 contribution this month

investments.title: Begin regular 401(k) contributions
investments.why: You hold $330,000 invested and $250,000 in 401(k)s but contributions are $0 today; employer matches matter.
steps: Confirm each employer’s match details with HR or plan documents
Choose a recurring payroll deferral amount in each 401(k) plan
Enable automatic contributions to start with the next paycheck
